At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

jobs.description:
Position:

Director of FP&A

Company:

Solen Software Group

Location:

Hybrid/On-site - Salt Lake City or Park City, New York, Toronto

Employment Type:

Full-time

About Solen Software Group

Solen Software Group is an evergreen holding company that acquires and operates proven software businesses that have significant growth potential in a variety of vertical markets, enabling them to be market leaders in their niche industry. Solen owns several software companies in various market spaces: Human Resource Technology, Fleet Telematics, Asset Management, E-Health, Document Management, and other innovative software solutions in a variety of industries. Solen is backed by a group of advisors and investors that have built software businesses of material scale (10-100M in ARR) and advised many.

About The Role

The Director of FP&A will own how Solen plans, forecasts, measures, and makes decisions across our portfolio of 20+ software companies and the holding company. Reporting to the CFO, this role partners as a peer with the Controller: the Controller owns the close, books, and consolidated actuals, while the Director of FP&A owns the budget, forecast, KPIs, Monthly Business Review, and the models behind capital allocation and acquisitions.

This is a build-as-you-go role. Our businesses run with real autonomy and span recurring SaaS, usage-based fees, professional services, and hardware. You will design the planning and reporting engine that replaces today's manual, company-by-company reporting, build the team that runs it, and support the CFO in raising debt and equity capital.

This is a highly strategic, hands-on leadership role working directly with the CFO, CEO, Portfolio Leaders, and General Managers of our operating companies (OpCos).

Key Responsibilities

Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting

Own the annual budget, quarterly re-forecast, rolling forecast, and long-range plan across all OpCos and the HoldCo, with one planning calendar and standard templates.
Build driver-based models suited to each revenue model: ARR, retention and churn cohorts, usage volumes, utilization and billable hours, hardware and license sales, and headcount.
Produce a consolidated, scenario-ready outlook for the CFO, CEO, and board.
Own forward cash forecasting and liquidity and covenant-headroom modelling in partnership with the Controller.
Track forecast accuracy, explain material misses, and continuously improve the process.

Portfolio Performance & KPIs

Define and deploy a consistent KPI framework across the portfolio, benchmarked against Solen's investment thesis.
Track unit economics, retention cohorts, customer profitability, and cost structure by function to benchmark OpCos against each other and best-in-class.
Support OpCo leaders on pricing, customer profitability, cost optimization, and financial turnarounds.

Monthly Business Review & Reporting

Own the MBR cadence, structure, KPI package, and follow-through on action items, raising the quality of insight in every review.
Partner with divisional controllers who run OpCo-level MBRs, equipping them with better data, tools, and insight.
Standardize and automate management reporting and dashboards in Power BI, and develop digital, real-time, and AI-native reporting.
Own the reporting roadmap, defining every metric once and building core reports such as the ARR bridge, budget-versus-actual, organic versus inorganic growth, EBITDA bridge, free cash flow, 13-week cash forecast, and return on invested capital.

Capital Allocation, Capital Raising & M&A

Build the models that guide capital allocation across reinvestment, bolt-on acquisitions, and cash returned to the HoldCo.
Support the CFO and deal team with acquisition models: valuation, diligence, pro formas, and synergy cases.
Support the CFO on debt and equity raises and refinancing with models, projections, scenario analysis, and lender and investor materials.
Track post-acquisition performance against the underwriting case and onboard new acquisitions into planning and KPIs from day one.

FP&A Team Build-Out

Design the FP&A operating model for a lean, decentralized portfolio.
Recruit, hire, and develop a best-in-class FP&A and business partner team.
Establish clear ownership between FP&A, the Controller, divisional controllers, and OpCo finance leaders.
Foster a culture of ownership, candor, and continuous improvement.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, accounting, or a related field; MBA or CFA preferred.
8+ years of progressive FP&A, corporate finance, or strategic finance experience.
Direct ownership of budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning for a multi-entity or decentralized business (e.g., PE-backed platform, roll-up, or multi-brand company).
Experience building, leading, and developing an FP&A or business partner team.
Excellent financial modelling skills, including driver-based forecasting and scenario analysis; advanced Excel.
Experience designing KPI frameworks and running recurring business reviews with operating leaders.
Experience building management reporting and dashboards in a BI tool.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to turn complex analysis into clear recommendations for a CEO, board, or non-finance operator.
Willing to work on-site in Salt Lake City or Park City, UT, or in New York, NY with regular travel to Utah, and occasional international travel to Lisbon, Portugal.
Legally authorized to work in the United States.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in B2B or vertical market SaaS, including ARR, GRR/NRR, and cohort analysis.
Experience modelling mixed revenue streams: subscription, usage-based, professional services, and hardware.
Background in private equity, permanent capital, investment banking, or Big-4 transaction advisory.
Experience supporting debt or equity raises or refinancing.
Experience using AI tools to automate manual finance work.
Working knowledge of Power BI and Sage Intacct or a comparable multi-entity ERP.
Experience with multi-currency planning and teams based outside the U.S.

Not every candidate will meet every requirement. If you have shown real trajectory and results, we encourage you to apply.

What Success Looks Like

One planning and forecasting engine is live across all OpCos and the HoldCo, with a full budget cycle and rolling forecast completed and forecast accuracy improving.
A consistent KPI framework is adopted by every OpCo, with each company viewed on one comparable scorecard against Solen's investment thesis.
The MBR runs on a predictable cadence with a standardized, automated package, and the highest-priority reports are live.
The FP&A function is defined, first hires are ramping, and manual reporting has come off the accounting team.
Capital allocation, acquisition, and financing models exist and have informed real decisions.
The CFO, CEO, Portfolio Leaders, and GMs seek FP&A's view before major decisions.

Solen-isms (How We Operate)

Ownership Mindset: We own the mission. We don't wait to be told. We lead, fix, and build as if it were ours. When problems arise, we run toward them, not away.
Benchmark to Best: We seek out excellence. We measure ourselves against the best and adapt quickly, always looking for the edge that moves us forward.
Openly Self-Critical: Leaders go first: they surface their misses early, ask for direct feedback, and turn “game film” into better decisions and better systems.
Disagree & Commit: Leaders disagree openly and constructively, regardless of title or tenure, because truth is how we avoid bureaucracy and benchmark to best.
Figureitoutiveness: Embracing challenges, fostering growth, and taking initiative, leaders thrive on hard work and high failure tolerance.
Mutual Elevation: Committed to growth, elevating teams, developing future leaders, and removing barriers to mastery and joy.
Learn-it-alls: Learn-it-alls, not know-it-alls, embracing failure as part of growth and progress.
Pioneering: Pioneering driven by opportunity, using first principles thinking and unbound by tradition or rules.
Will to Win: Leaders relentlessly pursue potential, reject mediocrity, and get what they tolerate.
Dialectical: We learn through conversation. We ask, listen, question, and evolve — valuing disagreement as a tool for alignment and deeper understanding.
Frugality: Achieving more with less, focusing on quality, long-term value, and company-wide responsibility.
Candor: We communicate with integrity, transparency, and respect in all conversations.
Kaizen: Kaizen is continuous improvement as a way of life. Leaders make hundreds of small upgrades that compound, turning lessons into standards and standards into durable systems.

Recruitment Disclaimer

Solen Software Group will never request payment, banking information, or other sensitive personal or financial details during any stage of the recruitment process. All official communication will come from a verified @solensoftwaregroup.com email address. Any outreach outside these standards should be disregarded and reported through our official channels.

We thank all applicants for their interest in joining Solen Software Group. Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

About AISI

AstraZeneca AI for Science Innovation (AISI) is driving the convergence of artificial intelligence and life sciences at enterprise scale. AISI brings together data foundations, AI and machine-learning technology, strategic partnerships, process reinvention, and business-facing AI to accelerate drug discovery, development, and delivery. Success depends on connecting and scaling existing capabilities, promoting reuse, and translating innovation into measurable scientific, patient, and enterprise value.

The Opportunity

The Director, Portfolio Management will lead the design, governance, and continuous improvement of AISI's portfolio management capability across strategic initiatives, AI and data platforms, external partnerships, projects, suppliers, managed services, and operational investments. The role ensures that strategy is translated into an executable portfolio, investments and resources are directed to the highest-value opportunities, delivery performance is transparent, and financial and operational risk, and compliance governance are embedded throughout the portfolio lifecycle.

Operating at the intersection of AISI leadership, scientific and therapeutic-area stakeholders, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, Procurement, HR, and external partners, the Director will establish scalable ways of working, strengthen evidence-based decision-making, and deliver outcomes through cross-functional teams and managed-service providers. The role sits within AISI Operations and reports to the Head of AISI Operations.

Scope And Core Accountabilities

Portfolio Strategy, Planning, and Governance

Translate AISI strategy and scientific priorities into an integrated portfolio of investments, initiatives, platforms, products, partnerships, and operational services.
Establish and continuously improve demand intake, assessment, value-based prioritization, funding, resource allocation, stage-gate review, delivery assurance, and benefits-realization processes.
Maintain an integrated portfolio view, identifying opportunities to stop, sequence, accelerate, consolidate, reuse, or scale initiatives as priorities and evidence evolve.
Lead portfolio governance forums and provide clear executive reporting on investment, demand, delivery health, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, capacity, financial performance, and expected value.
Develop standardized dashboards and management information that enable timely, transparent, evidence-based decisions without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

Financial and Investment Management

Oversee forecast-versus-budget analysis, variance management, accruals, cross-charges, resource recharges, purchase orders, and supplier-related financial commitments.
Ensure financial information is accurate, timely, transparent, and connected to portfolio priorities, delivery milestones, and benefits realization.
Define and track financial and non-financial value measures, including scientific impact, speed, adoption, reuse, risk reduction, productivity, and enterprise scalability.

Operating Model and Process Excellence

Design and evolve the portfolio operating model, decision rights, governance forums, escalation pathways, and RACI frameworks required to manage a complex, global portfolio.
Drive standardization, simplification, automation, and continuous improvement across portfolio, project, financial, supplier, contracting, resource, onboarding, and service-management processes.
Introduce fit-for-purpose Agile, Lean Portfolio Management, Design Thinking, incremental delivery, and hybrid governance practices where appropriate.
Ensure processes are practical, adopted, and supported by reliable data and fit-for-purpose tools, including ServiceNow, Azure DevOps, and portfolio or financial-management platforms.

Partnership, Contracting, and Supplier Governance

Provide end-to-end portfolio oversight of strategic alliances, AI and data partnerships, technology providers, suppliers, and managed services.
Partner with Legal, Procurement, Finance, Privacy, Information Security, and technical leaders across the contracting lifecycle, from intake, due diligence, term-sheet development, and negotiation through execution, performance review, renewal, and exit.
Implement supplier and partner governance through scorecards, service-level agreements, periodic business reviews, delivery-quality measures, commercial-health monitoring, risk mitigation, and value-for-money assessments.
Ensure partner commitments, dependencies, milestones, financial obligations, and benefits are integrated into portfolio planning and reporting.

Resource and Capacity Management

Lead resource and capacity-management practices across projects, products, platforms, partnerships, and operational services.
Oversee workforce planning, allocation, utilization, people recharges, onboarding, and prioritization of scarce scientific, AI, engineering, and portfolio-management capabilities.
Work with functional leaders to identify capability gaps, resolve constraints, improve onboarding, and align internal and external capacity with strategic priorities.

Risk, Compliance, and Delivery Assurance

Establish portfolio-level approaches to risk, issue, dependency, assumption, and decision management, ensuring material concerns are identified early, escalated appropriately, and managed through resolution.
Provide oversight of scope, schedule, cost, quality, benefits, adoption, operational readiness, and delivery performance across the portfolio.
Ensure portfolio activities and external arrangements comply with relevant pharmaceutical and technology requirements, including data governance, GDPR and privacy, information security, intellectual property, procurement, ethical, quality, and regulatory frameworks.
Anticipate and manage delivery underperformance, supplier failure, commercial disputes, IP complexity, changing priorities, financial pressure, data and technology dependencies, and regulatory constraints.

Facilitate alignment on priorities, investment choices, delivery expectations, trade-offs, and accountabilities across a global matrix organization.
Communicate complex portfolio, financial, commercial, and delivery matters clearly to senior leaders and diverse stakeholder groups.
Champion adoption of portfolio standards, transparent governance, and collaborative delivery while preserving the speed and experimentation required for AI innovation.

Leadership

Create a culture of accountability, collaboration, customer focus, continuous improvement, reuse, and measurable value delivery.
Set clear standards and build scalable capabilities from the ground up, enabling consistent ways of working across functions and geographies.

Essential

About Jetson

Jetson is on a mission to accelerate the transition of 100 million homes across North America away from fossil fuels toward sustainable energy use. We believe in a future that is 100% electric and 100% better.

Homes are one of the largest sources of carbon emissions, yet adoption of solutions like heat pumps remains slow due to cost and complexity. Jetson is solving this by building the first fully vertically integrated home electrification company — making clean energy simple, transparent, and affordable.

We rely heavily on technology, automation, and data to scale this impact. At Jetson, we value people who are excellent at their craft, curious about new tools (including AI), and motivated to continuously improve how work gets done.

The Opportunity:

We are looking for a Director of Supply Chain Programs to build and lead programs that connect Jetson's products to their full life in the field. Jetson's product portfolio is expanding fast, and every new product needs to arrive in the field supply-chain-ready and stay supported once it's installed. Reporting to the VP of Supply Chain & Warehousing, you own Supply Chain's side of the product lifecycle: from engineering handoff through sourcing, planning, stocking, and field launch, and then through service parts, warranty, and returns for the life of the installed base. Both programs are early — Supply Chain's NPI process is a lightweight framework still taking shape, and Service has little more than a list of commonly replaced parts. This is a director-level, build-it-yourself role: you'll design the processes, cadence, and metrics, rally cross-functional partners who don't report to you, and grow a team as the need is proven out.

What You Will Do:

Overall

Operate at the level this role requires: take general, intent-based guidance and turn it into comprehensive results; bring order out of chaos; be strategic in how you approach problems while staying highly effective in tactical moments; lean into areas of need as a self-starter without waiting to be directed; and bring a mature, seasoned presence to every situation ranging from a warehouse floor to an executive readout.
Lead and manage your direct reports as the team grows — setting priorities, developing their skills, and maintaining full situational awareness of every product in flight and every active service issue, so nothing is a surprise to you or to leadership.
Know the full portfolio well enough to speak to status, risk, and next steps on any NPI or Service workstream at any time — not just the ones on your desk that week.
Deliver regular formal and informal updates — from a quick heads-up as something comes up to a structured leadership brief — so progress, risk, and blockers stay visible between scheduled checkpoints, not just at them.
Facilitate updates and conversations with stakeholders across the business that are clear, concise, accurate, and customer-centric — translating product and service complexity into language that lands with the audience in front of you.
Maintain an informative, easy-to-navigate repository for programs — launch plans, readiness status, service parts data, and decisions — using dashboards, Notion, and other tools, so anyone can find current status, documentation, and history without having to ask you directly.

New Product Introduction

Own Supply Chain's side of every new product introduction, from engineering and product handoff through supply chain readiness and field launch. Work alongside Product and Engineering, who own product development, and orchestrate Procurement, Planning, Systems, Supply Chain Operations, and field teams.
Build on Supply Chain's existing NPI framework to develop its playbook and stage-gate readiness criteria: BOM release and item setup in Arena and NetSuite, supplier quality and industrialization (with Procurement), certification and compliance, first articles, packaging and labeling, stocking plans, warehouse and 3PL readiness, and field training.
Partner with Procurement on supplier quality and industrialization for new products, setting the readiness criteria and staying involved through qualification, first articles, and the move from pilot to production.
Serve as Supply Chain's primary partner to Product and Engineering — engaged early in the development process so supply chain constraints, cost, lead times, and serviceability shape decisions before they are locked.
Work with Procurement and Jetson's in-region sourcing partners to keep development milestones, certification, and supply readiness at key contract manufacturers aligned and visible to Jetson leadership.
Represent the new-product pipeline in Jetson's Integrated Business Planning (IBP) cycle — the coordinator who brings launch timing, ramp volumes, and risks into the demand and supply plan before they land in the execution horizon.
Run NPI program cadence and reporting from the supply chain perspective — timelines, readiness status, risks, and decisions — so leadership has one current view of every product in flight.

Service

Build and own Jetson's Service supply chain from the ground up — the processes, data flows, signals, and reporting that keep installed systems running and customers whole.
Define the service parts portfolio: identify and structure commonly replaced parts by product and platform, with clean part numbers, BOM linkages, and supersession rules.
Design the service parts stocking and fulfillment model — including forward-stocking critical parts at warehouse and 3PL locations so technicians can get the right part fast — partnering with Planning on stocking levels and Supply Chain Operations on execution.
Establish service consumption signals and demand history so service parts are planned by the system rather than by memory, partnering with Planning & Systems on NetSuite and field-service system integration.
Own warranty and returns processes: claims, RMAs, failure analysis, and disposition of returned or defective material. Partner with Procurement on supplier cost recovery, and feed field failure trends back to Engineering, Product, and Supplier Quality.
Build Service reporting that gives leadership visibility into claim volumes, resolution time, parts availability, cost trends, and failure rates by product and supplier.

What You Bring:

5+ years of program management or supply chain leadership experience in hardware, durable goods, HVAC, energy, or similar physical products, including ownership of NPI or product launch programs.
Experience building or running service parts, aftermarket, warranty, or reverse logistics programs — ideally including standing one up where little formal structure existed.
A proven program management track record with structured, cross-functional processes (stage-gate, launch readiness, RCCA, or similar); PMP or equivalent is a plus.
Working knowledge of ERP and PLM systems (NetSuite and Arena a plus) and how item, BOM, and service data flow through them.
Supplier- and partner-facing experience, including working with contract manufacturers and overseas suppliers on development, certification, and quality.
Cross-functional influence — you drive accountability and alignment across Product, Engineering, Procurement, Planning, Operations, and field teams without direct authority over most of them.
Strong analytical fluency and executive presence — able to turn program status and service data into a clear narrative and decisions for senior leadership.
Comfort operating in a fast-scaling, still-forming organization where scope shifts, teams are lean, and everyone pitches in.
Experience with modern tools, including AI, to automate and make your day more efficient.

Role Description

As the Director, Insights & Measurement
, you will be the primary analytical mind and strategic architect behind our advanced media attribution, experimentation, and business science methodologies. This role is designed for a heavyweight statistician and media measurement expert who thrives on solving the "what worked and why" for major brands.

While you will collaborate closely with our dedicated internal Data Engineering and Infrastructure teams—who build and maintain our cloud pipelines—you will own the frameworks, model designs, and causal inference methodologies. You will act as a senior leader, serving as the crucial bridge who translates complex statistical outputs (like MMM, MTA, and lift studies) into high-level strategic narratives and multi-million-dollar budget optimization recommendations for modern CMOs and CFOs.

Location: Toronto
Core Focus: 70% Attribution Methodology & Experimental Design; 30% Client Consulting, Narrative Strategy & Team Mentorship.

Advanced Attribution & Econometric Modeling

Methodology Ownership: Lead the theoretical design, validation of custom Marketing Mix Models (MMM), Multi-Touch Attribution (MTA), and customer Path-to-Conversion frameworks.
Unified Measurement Strategy: Champion a "Unified Measurement" approach, combining macro-level MMM econometric trends with micro-level digital attribution signals to give clients a singular source of truth.
Advanced Feature Engineering & Design: Determine the data requirements, adstock transformations, and saturation curve variables needed for accurate modelling, directing data engineers on how to prepare these schemas.

Experimentation & Causal Inference

Testing Frameworks: Architect randomized control trials (RCTs), matched-market tests, and geo-lift studies to establish true incrementality and validate marketing models.

Our ideal candidate is an intellectually curious and commercially minded research leader who combines methodological excellence with strategic thinking, client advisory skills, and a passion for turning evidence into action.

This is a highly quantitative role. Candidates must possess significant hands-on experience designing, executing, and interpreting advanced quantitative research studies and analyses. Individuals whose experience is primarily qualitative should not apply.

Translate client issues and strategic questions into learning agendas, testable hypotheses, and robust research methodologies.
Apply advanced analytical techniques and methodological best practices to ensure research is insightful, innovative, and fit for purpose.

Team. Assess current capability, design the team structure, and recruit, develop and retain the category management, sourcing and procurement operations talent the function needs. Build the skills, career paths and performance standards that make procurement a destination role at Xplore.

jobs.title: Director, Capital Projects
jobs.description:
Cyclic Materials is building a resilient circular supply chain for rare earth elements and other critical materials. Through our fully integrated proprietary technology platform, we recover rare earths from end-of-life products and transform them into high-purity materials used to produce new permanent magnets. These magnets are critical to the modern economy, underpinning AI, automotive, e-mobility, electronics, semiconductor, energy, defense, and other advanced manufacturing sectors.

Founded in 2021, Cyclic Materials has rapidly become a category leader in rare earth recovery, achieving commercial operations in less than five years. We currently operate facilities in Ontario and Arizona, with further expansion underway in South Carolina. Backed by investment accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc., alongside strategic investors including Microsoft, Amazon, Hitachi Ventures, BMW i Ventures, Jaguar Land Rover’s InMotion fund, Energy Impact Partners, ArcTern Ventures, and Fifth Wall, we are scaling quickly and building the industrial backbone required to meet growing global demand for a secure and sustainable supply of rare earths.

We have established an extensive and growing network of commercial partnerships with global industry leaders such as Solvay, Vattenfall, Lime, and VACUUMSCHMELZE, enabling the rapid deployment of recycled rare earth materials into real-world supply chains. Joining Cyclic Materials means tackling complex and exciting challenges at scale alongside a team committed to strong execution and measurable impact. If you are motivated by building critical infrastructure and advancing the circular economy, join us and help accelerate the growth of rare earth recycling.
The Director, Capital Projects leads domestic and international capital projects for rare earth element recycling and recovery, from planning and site selection through engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, start-up, and operational
handover. Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Capital Projects, Engineering & Procurement, this role ensures projects are delivered safely, on time, within scope, and on budget while meeting technical, commercial, regulatory, and strategic objectives.
The ideal candidate brings strong leadership, strategic planning, contract negotiation, engineering, and cross-functional execution experience in a global industrial environment, with the ability to navigate complex technical, commercial, regulatory, legal, and cultural challenges in a fast-paced start-up setting. The role follows a hybrid work model, with 4 days per week in the office and 1 day per week working from home. Domestic and international travel is expected to be approximately 50%, including travel to project sites, engineering offices, vendor facilities, construction locations, partner facilities, commissioning sites, and potential new facility locations.
Key Responsibilities
Global Capital Project Execution
Lead global capital projects from initiation through completion, ensuring alignment with company strategy, growth objectives, technical requirements, and commercial priorities.
Oversee complex plant development initiatives, including planning, site selection, engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, start-up, and operational handover.

Assess technologies that improve efficiency, recovery, throughput, safety, reliability, environmental performance, and operating costs while ensuring constructability, operability, maintainability, process safety, and commissioning readiness.

Coordinate with legal, finance, engineering, environmental, and local advisors to support due diligence, acquisition, leasing, and development decisions.

Contracts, Procurement, and Partner Oversight
Lead contract negotiation for engineering, procurement, construction, equipment supply, installation, commissioning, consulting, service, and vendor agreements.
Partner with legal, procurement, finance, and executive leadership to structure agreements that protect company interests and support successful delivery.
Evaluate and oversee contractors, suppliers, technology partners, trades, and subcontractors for capability, terms, schedules, risks, and performance.
Oversee procurement strategies for major equipment, long-lead items, specialized processing systems, materials, construction services, and commissioning support.

Governance, Risk, and Performance Control

Capture lessons learned, standardize execution practices, and document handover and operational readiness processes

Lead cross-functional collaboration across time zones, cultures, disciplines, and geographies.

Ensure compliance with company policies, laws, regulations, permitting requirements, environmental standards, occupational health and safety requirements, and best practices.

Maintain appropriate controls for chemical handling, hazardous materials, waste treatment, process safety, and environmental protection.

Related business, project delivery, or technical degrees may be considered with substantial industrial capital project experience.
International MBA or globally focused MBA preferred.

12–15+ years leading global or large-scale industrial capital projects, preferably in chemical processing, metals, recycling, mining, critical minerals, rare earths, battery materials, specialty chemicals, or advanced manufacturing.

Experience developing first-of-kind, next-of-kind, modular, or repeatable plant designs and supporting pilot-to-commercial scale-up.

About Jetson

Jetson is on a mission to accelerate the transition of 100 million homes across North America away from fossil fuels toward sustainable energy use. We believe in a future that is 100% electric and 100% better.

Homes are one of the largest sources of carbon emissions, yet adoption of solutions like heat pumps remains slow due to cost and complexity. Jetson is solving this by building the first fully vertically integrated home electrification company — making clean energy simple, transparent, and affordable.

We rely heavily on technology, automation, and data to scale this impact. At Jetson, we value people who are excellent at their craft, curious about new tools (including AI), and motivated to continuously improve how work gets done.

The Opportunity:

We are looking for a Director of Supply Chain Programs to build and lead programs that connect Jetson's products to their full life in the field. Jetson's product portfolio is expanding fast, and every new product needs to arrive in the field supply-chain-ready and stay supported once it's installed. Reporting to the VP of Supply Chain & Warehousing, you own Supply Chain's side of the product lifecycle: from engineering handoff through sourcing, planning, stocking, and field launch, and then through service parts, warranty, and returns for the life of the installed base. Both programs are early — Supply Chain's NPI process is a lightweight framework still taking shape, and Service has little more than a list of commonly replaced parts. This is a director-level, build-it-yourself role: you'll design the processes, cadence, and metrics, rally cross-functional partners who don't report to you, and grow a team as the need is proven out.

What You Will Do:

Overall

Operate at the level this role requires: take general, intent-based guidance and turn it into comprehensive results; bring order out of chaos; be strategic in how you approach problems while staying highly effective in tactical moments; lean into areas of need as a self-starter without waiting to be directed; and bring a mature, seasoned presence to every situation ranging from a warehouse floor to an executive readout.
Lead and manage your direct reports as the team grows — setting priorities, developing their skills, and maintaining full situational awareness of every product in flight and every active service issue, so nothing is a surprise to you or to leadership.
Know the full portfolio well enough to speak to status, risk, and next steps on any NPI or Service workstream at any time — not just the ones on your desk that week.
Deliver regular formal and informal updates — from a quick heads-up as something comes up to a structured leadership brief — so progress, risk, and blockers stay visible between scheduled checkpoints, not just at them.
Facilitate updates and conversations with stakeholders across the business that are clear, concise, accurate, and customer-centric — translating product and service complexity into language that lands with the audience in front of you.
Maintain an informative, easy-to-navigate repository for programs — launch plans, readiness status, service parts data, and decisions — using dashboards, Notion, and other tools, so anyone can find current status, documentation, and history without having to ask you directly.

New Product Introduction

Own Supply Chain's side of every new product introduction, from engineering and product handoff through supply chain readiness and field launch. Work alongside Product and Engineering, who own product development, and orchestrate Procurement, Planning, Systems, Supply Chain Operations, and field teams.
Build on Supply Chain's existing NPI framework to develop its playbook and stage-gate readiness criteria: BOM release and item setup in Arena and NetSuite, supplier quality and industrialization (with Procurement), certification and compliance, first articles, packaging and labeling, stocking plans, warehouse and 3PL readiness, and field training.
Partner with Procurement on supplier quality and industrialization for new products, setting the readiness criteria and staying involved through qualification, first articles, and the move from pilot to production.
Serve as Supply Chain's primary partner to Product and Engineering — engaged early in the development process so supply chain constraints, cost, lead times, and serviceability shape decisions before they are locked.
Work with Procurement and Jetson's in-region sourcing partners to keep development milestones, certification, and supply readiness at key contract manufacturers aligned and visible to Jetson leadership.
Represent the new-product pipeline in Jetson's Integrated Business Planning (IBP) cycle — the coordinator who brings launch timing, ramp volumes, and risks into the demand and supply plan before they land in the execution horizon.
Run NPI program cadence and reporting from the supply chain perspective — timelines, readiness status, risks, and decisions — so leadership has one current view of every product in flight.

Service

Build and own Jetson's Service supply chain from the ground up — the processes, data flows, signals, and reporting that keep installed systems running and customers whole.
Define the service parts portfolio: identify and structure commonly replaced parts by product and platform, with clean part numbers, BOM linkages, and supersession rules.
Design the service parts stocking and fulfillment model — including forward-stocking critical parts at warehouse and 3PL locations so technicians can get the right part fast — partnering with Planning on stocking levels and Supply Chain Operations on execution.
Establish service consumption signals and demand history so service parts are planned by the system rather than by memory, partnering with Planning & Systems on NetSuite and field-service system integration.
Own warranty and returns processes: claims, RMAs, failure analysis, and disposition of returned or defective material. Partner with Procurement on supplier cost recovery, and feed field failure trends back to Engineering, Product, and Supplier Quality.
Build Service reporting that gives leadership visibility into claim volumes, resolution time, parts availability, cost trends, and failure rates by product and supplier.

What You Bring:

5+ years of program management or supply chain leadership experience in hardware, durable goods, HVAC, energy, or similar physical products, including ownership of NPI or product launch programs.
Experience building or running service parts, aftermarket, warranty, or reverse logistics programs — ideally including standing one up where little formal structure existed.
A proven program management track record with structured, cross-functional processes (stage-gate, launch readiness, RCCA, or similar); PMP or equivalent is a plus.
Working knowledge of ERP and PLM systems (NetSuite and Arena a plus) and how item, BOM, and service data flow through them.
Supplier- and partner-facing experience, including working with contract manufacturers and overseas suppliers on development, certification, and quality.
Cross-functional influence — you drive accountability and alignment across Product, Engineering, Procurement, Planning, Operations, and field teams without direct authority over most of them.
Strong analytical fluency and executive presence — able to turn program status and service data into a clear narrative and decisions for senior leadership.
Comfort operating in a fast-scaling, still-forming organization where scope shifts, teams are lean, and everyone pitches in.
Experience with modern tools, including AI, to automate and make your day more efficient.

Benefits:

Dental Care, Vision Care & Life Insurance premiums fully paid by Jetson
Extended Health Care
Disability Insurance
Education Support

Equity

Work Location:
In person - North Vancouver, BC, with regular travel to Jetson team, warehouse, and market locations across the US and Canada, and periodic supplier travel.

new_jobs.title: Director of Procurement
new_jobs.description:
Xplore Inc. is Canada’s fibre, 5G and satellite broadband company for rural living. Xplore is committed to the relentless pursuit of an improved broadband experience for all Canadians. Xplore is building a world-class fibre optic and 5G wireless network to enable innovative broadband services for better every day rural living, for today and future generations.

Xplore is building a procurement function fit for a national telecommunications operator: disciplined spending, strong supplier relationships, strategic partnerships with the business, and strong governance over all external spend. The Director, Procurement will lead that build.

The successful candidate will be accountable for designing, standing up and then running Xplore's procurement capability end to end including the operating model and processes, team, the framework and the systems that underpin them. You will inherit pockets of good practice and a committed set of stakeholders, and you will be expected to turn those into a cohesive, scalable function within a defined roadmap.

Reporting to the Vice President, Strategic Supplier Partnerships, you will own tactical and strategic procurement across Xplore's network, technology, operations and corporate spend, and act as the company's senior authority on sourcing, contracting and supplier management.

Key Responsibilities Include

Build the procurement capability

Operating model. Define the target operating model for procurement at Xplore — scope, structure, decision rights and interfaces with Finance, Legal, Engineering, Network Operations, IT and the business units — and lead the roadmap to get there.
Process. Design and implement the end-to-end source-to-contract and procure-to-pay processes: demand planning, sourcing, evaluation, negotiation, contracting, purchase order management, receipting and supplier performance review. Document them, embed them and measure adherence.
Team. Assess current capability, design the team structure, and recruit, develop and retain the category management, sourcing and procurement operations talent the function needs. Build the skills, career paths and performance standards that make procurement a destination role at Xplore.
Governance. Establish the procurement governance framework: delegation of authority and approval thresholds, sourcing and tendering policy, contract standards, supplier onboarding and due diligence, conflict-of-interest and ethics controls, and the reporting cadence to the executive team and Board committees.
Systems and data. Own the procurement technology roadmap. Select, implement and drive adoption of sourcing, contract lifecycle management, supplier management and procure-to-pay tooling, integrated with Xplore's ERP and finance systems, with the data model and reporting to support spend visibility and control.
Roadmap and measurement. Define the maturity model and milestones for the function, report progress transparently, and adjust the build plan as the business evolves.

Run strategic and tactical procurement

Category management. Lead category strategies across network infrastructure (fibre, fixed wireless, satellite capacity and ground equipment, towers and structures, civil works and construction), network electronics and radio access, customer premises equipment, IT hardware, software and cloud, professional and managed services, logistics, fleet and facilities, and corporate indirect spend.
Sourcing and negotiation. Run competitive sourcing events — RFI, RFP, RFQ and reverse auctions — with rigorous total-cost-of-ownership evaluation, and lead complex, high-value negotiations on commercial terms, service levels, warranties, intellectual property and liability.
Contracting. In partnership with Legal, own the commercial terms of supply, master services, construction, licensing and capacity agreements; maintain the contract repository and manage renewals, amendments and obligations.
Supplier management. Build and maintain a supplier segmentation and performance management program — scorecards, quarterly business reviews, corrective action and continuous improvement — in close alignment with the Strategic Supplier Partnerships team's management of tier-one relationships.
Supply risk and resilience. Identify, assess and mitigate supply risk across the supplier base: financial health, concentration and single-source exposure, geopolitical and trade-compliance risk, lead times, cybersecurity and data-protection posture, and business continuity.
Value delivery. Set and deliver annual savings, cost-avoidance and working-capital targets; own spend analytics and ensure procurement data is accurate, complete and actionable for Finance and operational leaders.
Compliance. Ensure procurement activity complies with Canadian procurement, competition, trade, privacy and anti-corruption law, applicable federal and provincial program requirements (including funded broadband build obligations), and Xplore's own policies.

Lead and influence

Act as a trusted commercial advisor to the executive team and functional leaders, bringing procurement into decisions early rather than at the purchase-order stage.
Champion the value of structured procurement across the organisation and lead the change management needed to shift behaviours, adopt new processes and tools, and sustain them.
Represent Xplore externally with suppliers, industry bodies and peers, and bring market intelligence and best practice back into the business.
Model Xplore's values and build an inclusive, high-performing, accountable team.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

10+ years of progressive procurement, strategic sourcing or supply chain experience, including 5+ years leading a procurement function or major category portfolio at the senior manager or director level.
Telecommunications, network infrastructure or a comparable capital-intensive technology industry background, with direct experience sourcing network equipment, infrastructure construction and large managed-service or capacity agreements.
Demonstrated experience building or substantially transforming a procurement function, i.e., designing operating models, processes and governance, implementing procurement systems and growing a team
Proven track record of leading complex, multi-year, high-value negotiations and delivering measurable savings and risk reduction.
Strong command of contract law fundamentals, commercial terms and risk allocation, and experience working closely with in-house and external counsel.
Hands-on experience selecting and implementing procurement technology (source-to-pay, CLM, supplier management, spend analytics) integrated with ERP platforms.
Excellent financial and analytical skills, including TCO modelling, spend analysis and business-case development.
Outstanding stakeholder management, influence and communication skills up to executive level, with the resilience to lead change in a growing organisation.
Bachelor's degree in business, supply chain management, engineering, finance or a related field.

Preferred

Supply Chain Management Professional (SCMP) designation, CIPS, CPSM or equivalent; MBA or relevant graduate degree.
Experience in a rural or regional broadband operator, or with government-funded broadband programs and their procurement and reporting obligations.
Familiarity with ESG and supplier diversity requirements, Indigenous procurement considerations and modern-slavery reporting in Canada.
Bilingual English and French is an asset.
